item.text: {"question_id":"3B.4","answer":"During 2023, Germany’s institutional framework provided meaningful independent judicial correction and parliamentary scrutiny, but the supplied evidence does not establish that Scholz created or personally directed those institutions. Courts invalidated unlawful or disproportionate measures, including indiscriminate data retention, predictive-policing/data-mining laws, BAMF smartphone screening, and an excessive residential search; detention orders were also repeatedly reviewable and sometimes found unlawful (BATCH-0003-E008; BATCH-0010-E010; BATCH-0011-R01-E016; BATCH-0024-E003; BATCH-0011-R05-E012). Parliamentary oversight was active, with 21 question hours, 21 government inquiries, 1,458 small inquiries, and 45 current-affairs debates, although volume alone does not show compliance or correction (BATCH-0032-E018). The coalition government enacted independent asylum counselling and provided €20 million for 2023, while BAMF maintained interpreter standards and a complaint process that could terminate contracts (BATCH-0011-R01-E003; BATCH-0011-R03-E011; BATCH-0011-R02-E001). Implementation and remedy were materially incomplete: counselling funding was delayed and judged insufficient, access to reception centres depended on individual requests and local discretion, nationwide access was not guaranteed, and no 2023 counselling-availability data were available (BATCH-0011-R01-E003; BATCH-0011-R03-E011; BATCH-0011-R03-E012). Police-accountability evidence is adverse: 90% of 2,790 investigations into alleged unlawful police force in 2021 were discontinued, only 2% led to charges, and many victims reportedly faced barriers to obtaining redress, though the study was non-representative and not specific to a Scholz decision (BATCH-0006-E008). Similarly, earlier interpreter misconduct had not triggered reassessment of affected cases, and no 2023 complaint data were available (BATCH-0011-R02-E001). Overall, independent review functioned and sometimes corrected state action, but complaint access, implementation, discipline, compensation, and systematic victim remedy remain insufficiently demonstrated. The evidence supports a functioning but uneven oversight-and-remedy environment, with Scholz’s attribution limited chiefly to the federal legal and funding framework; courts, Länder, local authorities, and administrative bodies retained substantial independent or decentralized
